prompts.dev1: Ines snorts while checking sales data. She says, Ignore the guesswork and fix only the items where missing stock actually lost money.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks worried and asks if we should tweak everything because the stakeholder wants faster results to stop future worries.

answers.text: Let us adjust a few random items so we please the stakeholder and feel like we are doing something.
answers.feedback: Changing random things wastes effort and ignores the real data that shows exactly where the problem lies right now.

answers.text: The stakeholder is right so we will rewrite all stock rules immediately to satisfy their sudden demands perfectly.
answers.feedback: Changing everything without proof breaks trust and throws away good work while ignoring the actual evidence of what failed.

answers.text: We pick the single item with clear proof of loss and fix just that one thing first.
answers.feedback: This choice uses hard numbers to improve value without wasting time on guessing or changing too much at once.

prompts.dev1: Ines taps her phone screen while rolling her eyes. She says the payment gateway is broken and everyone needs to stop working on other features right now.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks worried and keeps apologizing for the delay. He asks if we can just fix the bug quickly so we can finish the whole shopping app today.

answers.text: Let us try to finish both the payment fix and some new features before we stop working today.
answers.feedback: Changing the goal midway confuses the team. You might start tasks that cannot be finished by the end of the time box.

answers.text: We focus only on fixing the payment bug to meet our single goal for this Sprint.
answers.feedback: This keeps the team united around one purpose. It allows us to deliver a usable product without breaking rules.

answers.text: Since the bug is annoying, let us ignore it and just promise to fix it next week after we build new screens.
answers.feedback: Ignoring a blocker destroys trust with users. You also break your own commitment to finish work within the agreed time.

prompts.dev1: Hey, I heard you told customers our wish list feature launches today. No one asked for that and we never discussed it.
prompts.dev2: Oh no, I feel terrible about this. I really want to fix things but I am so scared of breaking the team.

answers.text: Let us pause and inspect our current progress before we adapt a new plan together as a group.
answers.feedback: This answer uses inspection to stop hidden work and adaptation to fix the plan safely for everyone.

answers.text: You should ignore the customer complaint and just build whatever you think is best to keep moving fast.
answers.feedback: Ignoring feedback breaks transparency and creates a mess that will hurt the product and the team trust.

answers.text: Maybe we should just tell the customers we need more time since nobody asked you to make that promise.
answers.feedback: Delaying without a team decision hides the real problem and wastes valuable time on the project.

prompts.dev1: Ines leans back with a smirk. She says our return system is broken but laughs it off because everyone looks at her.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks worried and apologizes for asking, saying the refund data shows big problems that we should tell the users about now.

answers.text: Ignore Tobi's concerns and tell everyone the returns process works perfectly because we need to stay positive.
answers.feedback: Lying about broken features destroys trust and makes it much harder to fix real user problems later.

answers.text: Let us investigate the refund numbers quietly and just hope nothing goes wrong during the sprint.
answers.feedback: Hiding problems until you are sure creates more confusion and wastes valuable time for the whole group.

answers.text: Tell the team the real problem so we can fix it together without hiding anything.
answers.feedback: This builds trust and lets everyone solve the issue openly instead of pretending everything is fine.

prompts.dev1: Hey, delivery slots are failing too much. Ines says the code is broken but we need proof before changing anything.
prompts.dev2: The numbers show a pattern in failed deliveries. We should pick one fix based on that data instead of guessing.

answers.text: Let us try updating both the server and app together just in case.
answers.feedback: Changing too much at once hides which fix worked. This wastes time and confuses our progress.

answers.text: Ignore the data logs since Ines always complains about small details anyway.
answers.feedback: Ignoring facts leads to wrong decisions and hurts trust. Dismissing a teammate damages our team spirit.

answers.text: Pick the change backed by the delivery failure numbers first.
answers.feedback: This choice uses evidence to guide work. It respects Scrum rules by focusing on value and facts.

prompts.dev1: Hey, remember we promised a dark mode for checkout yesterday? I built it without asking because I thought it was easy.
prompts.dev2: I heard about that promise. It feels wrong to build something nobody asked for while ignoring our real problems with the code.

answers.text: Let us keep the dark mode for now but try to fix other issues later.
answers.feedback: Keeping a fake promise wastes time and prevents the team from solving the actual problems they face today.

answers.text: You made a mistake so you should stop working on this project immediately.
answers.feedback: Blaming one person destroys trust and stops the whole team from speaking up about future risks.

answers.text: Please tell us the truth about what you changed and if anyone wants it.
answers.feedback: This answer encourages honesty so the team can adjust their plan together without hiding mistakes.

prompts.dev1: Hey, we need a new coupon feature right now. Our current task list is full and this could make our goal impossible.
prompts.dev2: I am so sorry for the delay. We have a great idea for coupons but adding it now will hurt our plan.

answers.text: We can try the coupon change quickly since it only takes a few hours of work today.
answers.feedback: Changing the goal mid-sprint risks failing the rest of the planned tasks and goals.

answers.text: Let us just drop everything else to build this new coupon feature right away.
answers.feedback: Ignoring the current sprint goal will confuse the team and likely cause you to miss your deadline.

answers.text: Add that coupon idea to the backlog for the next sprint instead of changing us now.
answers.feedback: This keeps the current sprint safe while saving the new idea for later.

prompts.dev1: I hate this. We should stop now because we cannot agree on the design for the checkout page.
prompts.dev2: Sorry, I feel bad too. Maybe we just need more time to figure out exactly what we want.

answers.text: We can try to do both ideas at once so everyone feels happy about their changes.
answers.feedback: Doing two things at once will confuse everyone and make it impossible to finish any useful work in time.

answers.text: Since we cannot agree now, we should just cancel this short time box and wait for later.
answers.feedback: Stopping early wastes all the progress made so far and breaks the promise of delivering a working part soon.

answers.text: Let us pick one goal first then work hard together to finish it by the end.
answers.feedback: This keeps the team focused on a single target and respects the fixed limit of the short time box.

prompts.dev1: Hey, I know Ines is being dry about order tracking. The system looks messy and we need clarity fast.
prompts.dev2: Tobi feels anxious because the work is unclear. He apologizes for asking too many questions while trying to understand how to track orders.

answers.text: Let us inspect this work together and adapt our plan based on what we see right now.
answers.feedback: This answer encourages inspection and adaptation by focusing on the actual work instead of blaming people or rushing.

answers.text: Ines is always sarcastic so you should just do whatever she says about the order tracking feature.
answers.feedback: Ignoring transparent discussion or blindly following one voice stops the team from inspecting reality and adapting their approach correctly.

answers.text: We should just skip this event for now since the work looks too confusing to finish today.
answers.feedback: Skipping the event ignores the need for transparency and fails to help the team inspect their current progress properly.

prompts.dev1: Hey, I finished these coupon features but they have bugs. Can we ship them so others see our progress?
prompts.dev2: Ines wants to finish early but Tobi worries about breaking things. Our last app had too many errors.

answers.text: We must not ship incomplete work until every item passes our Definition of Done checklist.
answers.feedback: This keeps the product usable and builds trust with users while preventing future technical debt.

answers.text: Let us ship just the fixed parts now and ignore the small bugs for the next sprint.
answers.feedback: Skipping issues creates a false sense of completion and leads to more problems later on.

answers.text: Okay, let us publish the broken features today since management is watching our sprint board closely.
answers.feedback: Releasing buggy software damages user trust and violates the rule that only working software counts.

prompts.dev1: Ines rolls her eyes at the stakeholder request. She says we are already late and adding this now is a bad idea.
prompts.dev2: Tobi worries that ignoring the stakeholder will hurt our relationship. He asks if we can try to fix the process without changing the code right now.

answers.text: We can quickly add a feature to handle returns if we cut something else out today.
answers.feedback: Changing work mid-sprint often leads to confusion and delays because it breaks the original plan.

answers.text: Fine, let us stop everything right now to build exactly what the stakeholder wants immediately.
answers.feedback: This destroys trust by ignoring team agreements and throws away all progress made so far this week.

answers.text: Let us finish our current work first, then discuss new ideas in our next meeting.
answers.feedback: This keeps the team focused on finishing their tasks before accepting outside changes during the sprint.

prompts.dev1: Hey, I found a great review idea. Can we add it now? It will make Amazin better for our users right away.
prompts.dev2: Tobi is worried the new code might break our shopping cart. He asks if you can stop the current work to fix their big idea.

answers.text: We cannot change goals mid-sprint. Let us write this new review idea on the list for next time.
answers.feedback: This protects the current plan while saving the good idea for later safe work.

answers.text: We can try to add it now but we might run out of time before the end.
answers.feedback: Trying risky changes often causes stress and delays without actually finishing the main goal properly.

answers.text: Great idea, let us cancel everything else and start building this new review feature immediately today.
answers.feedback: Stopping now destroys all progress made so far and leaves the team without a clear plan.

samples.title: Picking a clear aim for users

prompts.dev1: Ines sighs while looking at our task list. She says we keep adding tiny features instead of finishing something real for shoppers.
prompts.dev2: Tobi nervously explains that everyone is confused because we only listed tasks but no one knows what to build together today.

answers.text: Forget the user needs and just finish whatever small tasks were written in our original list.
answers.feedback: Ignoring what users want causes frustration and wastes time on work that does not help anyone.

answers.text: Maybe we can finish both the credit card part and the gift card option if we hurry.
answers.feedback: Trying to do too many things often leads to confusion and rushing quality down for everyone involved.

answers.text: Let us focus on letting users pay with any card smoothly by this week.
answers.feedback: This answer picks a clear outcome for people using the app instead of just listing work items.

prompts.dev1: Ines checks the code and laughs. She says the slow validation step is unnecessary and suggests skipping it to finish faster.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks worried about the risk. He admits he feels nervous but agrees with Ines because everyone wants to launch soon.

answers.text: We must verify every input to protect user data even if it slows us down today.
answers.feedback: This choice honors truth and safety, ensuring the product remains reliable despite the temptation to cut corners.

answers.text: Great idea, Ines! We will remove the check completely and hope no one notices the errors later.
answers.feedback: Hiding problems creates debt and breaks trust with users. This action directly violates our core values of honesty.

answers.text: Let us skip validation only for this one test user so we can finish the launch quickly.
answers.feedback: Testing on one user is not enough. This partial fix ignores the real risk that affects all customers.

prompts.dev1: Ines leans back and says our coupon list is broken. She thinks we are wasting time fixing small glitches instead of shipping the app.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks worried and asks if anyone knows how to fix the block since he keeps forgetting his own tasks and feeling guilty.

answers.text: I think we should wait until tomorrow when everyone is less tired and the code might fix itself.
answers.feedback: Waiting ignores the need for immediate inspection and allows the block to grow larger while no one adapts.

answers.text: Let us inspect the code together right now so we can adapt and remove this block safely.
answers.feedback: This answer uses inspection to see the problem clearly, then adapts the plan to move forward quickly.

answers.text: Since Ines was sarcastic earlier, she probably broke it on purpose so we will have to reset everything.
answers.feedback: Blaming a teammate destroys transparency and stops inspection because fear prevents the team from looking at real causes.

prompts.dev1: Hey, we are almost done with the checkout page. Ines says the payment logic is tricky but doable.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks worried because a bug just appeared and she feels guilty about it not being fixed yet.

answers.text: Tell Tobi to share the bug now so we can fix it before the sprint ends today.
answers.feedback: This keeps progress honest and small. It prevents hidden problems from growing out of control later.

answers.text: We should just hide the bug for now since the review is happening tomorrow morning anyway.
answers.feedback: Hiding issues only makes them bigger. Small delays today will cause big failures during the final review.

answers.text: Tell Tobi to quit because she keeps finding problems and slowing down our fast progress on checkout.
answers.feedback: This destroys trust and stops honest communication. You would force people to lie about their real work.

prompts.dev1: Ines leans back, eyes dry. That new loyalty points feature was promised by a client last hour. The team agreed to the shopping cart goal without debate.
prompts.dev2: Tobi looks nervous and holds their head low. They say sorry again because they feel bad that someone made a promise we did not plan for this sprint.

answers.text: Ask the developer who built it to try adding it tonight even if the code feels unstable.
answers.feedback: Trying to force unfinished work in risks breaking your current goal and burning out everyone on the team.

answers.text: Tell the client we must cancel our original shopping cart goal to build their requested loyalty points feature now.
answers.feedback: Abandoning a committed goal mid-sprint destroys trust and creates chaos that delays all future work significantly.

answers.text: Tell the client to move the idea to the backlog for next sprint instead of starting now.
answers.feedback: This keeps our goal safe and respects the team agreement while still saving the new idea for later.

prompts.dev1: We promised the client a dark mode next week. I didn't talk to anyone about it and now we are short on time.
prompts.dev2: I was nervous so I stayed quiet. Now Ines looks mad because she knows we lied to the client without telling her first.

answers.text: We should blame Ines for complaining so we can finish our own secret plan without any trouble.
answers.feedback: Blaming a teammate destroys trust and stops honest conversation which is needed to solve real problems effectively.

answers.text: We must tell the client the truth now and explain our plan to fix it together.
answers.feedback: This answer builds trust by being honest about the mistake and inviting the team to solve the problem.

answers.text: Let us try to finish the light version first and hope the client does not notice.
answers.feedback: Hiding the truth creates more stress later when the deadline is missed or the client finds out anyway.

prompts.dev1: I told you the stock feature is done. It runs fast and looks good. I fixed it myself without asking anyone.
prompts.dev2: I feel bad about that Ines. We agreed to check code together but I did not stop her from finishing alone.

answers.text: Let us finish coding the rest of the feature today to make up for the delay.
answers.feedback: Adding more work now ignores the quality gap that already exists in the codebase.

answers.text: Great job Ines. Just merge this into main and let us celebrate the quick win.
answers.feedback: Accepting unfinished work sets a bad example that causes bigger problems later on.

answers.text: We must mark the task as not done until we review it together with everyone.
answers.feedback: This keeps work transparent and prevents hidden issues from hurting future sprints.

prompts.dev1: Hey, I just realized we hit a big roadblock with the gift card feature before our deadline.
prompts.dev2: This is so bad. I feel terrible that we might not finish our goal for this sprint.

answers.text: Let us focus only on getting gift cards to work perfectly by tomorrow.
answers.feedback: This keeps the team focused on one clear goal and lets you fix the problem without panic.

answers.text: Forget the goal for now and let us start building whatever new idea you have instead.
answers.feedback: Changing goals mid-sprint confuses everyone and wastes time because you lose your agreed-upon target for this week.

answers.text: We can try to finish half of the gift card feature if we just rush a bit.
answers.feedback: Rushing leads to mistakes and breaks your promise to deliver a complete, working product for everyone.

intros.dev1: Empty carts claim to have items. I have been staring at it too long. Your turn.
intros.dev2: Um, an empty cart says it has items. I am stuck, sorry. Could you find the line?

intros.dev1: Night owls get a surcharge. The code charges zero instead. Please fix the logic so it charges four.
intros.dev2: Oh no, I think the fee is backwards. It says zero for night mode but should say four. Can you help?

intros.dev1: I checked the receipt again. It says members save five dollars, but the math here is completely wrong.
intros.dev2: Oh no! I am sorry for my confusion. The price should drop for members, but right now it stays high.

intros.dev1: Shelves are empty but the tag screams full. I need a break from this nonsense logic.
intros.dev2: Oh no, the labels are backwards! I tried fixing it but the code still lies to us.

intros.dev1: Members are supposed to save money, but the math is backwards today. Please fix the calculation logic.
intros.dev2: Oh no! The code gives wrong prices sometimes. I tried hard but forgot how to use minus signs properly.

intros.dev1: Discounts apply to members only. I see you subtracted it for everyone anyway. Please fix that logic.
intros.dev2: Oh no, the math is wrong for regular folks. They shouldn't pay less at all! Can you help?

intros.dev1: Express ships claim to be slow. I have been staring at it too long. Your turn.
intros.dev2: Um, an express ship says it is standard speed. I am stuck, sorry. Could you find the line?

intros.dev1: Night hours charge nothing. I checked the code and the fee calculation is backwards. Please fix it.
intros.dev2: Oh no, the night fee function is giving zero dollars instead of four. I am so sorry for my mistake.

intros.dev1: Member discounts are broken. I keep seeing regular prices for everyone. Please fix the math here.
intros.dev2: Oh no! The discount isn't working at all. Could you look at the code and help me fix it?

intros.dev1: Expired coupons claim to be valid. I have been staring at it too long. Your turn.
intros.dev2: Um, an expired coupon says it is valid. I am stuck, sorry. Could you find the line?
